back: A high-gain voltage amplifier with an inverting (−) and a non-inverting (+) input whose output depends on the difference between the input voltages.
$V_{\text{out}} = A_0(V^{+} - V^{-})$, limited to $\pm V_{\text{sat}}$ (about the supply voltages)
Infinite open-loop gain, input resistance, bandwidth and slew rate; zero output resistance.
$A_0 \approx 2 \times 10^{5}$; input resistance $\approx 2\ \text{M}\Omega$; output resistance $\approx 75\ \Omega$; slew rate $\approx 0.5\ \text{V}\,\mu\text{s}^{-1}$.
The output has reached (nearly) a supply voltage and cannot rise further, whatever the input difference.
The maximum rate of change of the output voltage of an op-amp (V µs⁻¹).
No feedback: output +V_sat when V⁺ > V⁻ and −V_sat when V⁺ < V⁻. A sensor divider on one input and a reference divider on the other set the switching point.
The op-amp draws no current from a sensor divider, so it does not change the voltage it is measuring.
A diode across the relay coil carries the current from the large e.m.f. induced when the coil is switched off, protecting the op-amp.
